messages:
emma-support: FYI AcmeHealth is reporting a sudden wave of 503s on hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. Customer says it started after a large batch embed job. Repro steps and logs below, tagging SRE.

acmeops-customer: seeing ~20% of requests 503 gateway, streaming endpoints return 'STREAM_RESET' and non-stream endpoints get 503. No change from our side other than ramping to 250 concurrent embed requests.

emma-support: Repro steps they provided: 1) POST /v1/embeddings with batch size 512, 2) http2 multiplexing enabled in SDK (default), 3) region: us-west2, model: open-embed-v2, 4) concurrency ~250.

emma-support: Logs snippet from customer: ```
error: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = upstream response error: 503 
http2: stream error: stream ID 12345; INTERNAL_ERROR
upstream: connection reset by peer
```

marta-eng-infra: Thanks — initial check of edge proxies in us-west2 shows ingress connection queue depth spike at 09:09-09:13 and many h2 GOAWAYs. See grafana: https://grafana.redwood/edge/conn-queue?range=09:00-09:30 (shared privately).

raj-eng-sre: @marta-eng-infra can you check worker pool CPU/ephemeral port saturation too? This smells like http2 stream window exhaustion + client retry amplification. Also, did they use SDK default retry (which may fanout on 5xx)?

emma-support: They included SDK settings: "max_concurrency": 0 (no limit), http2 multiplexing true, retry backoff: default.

kai-devex: Quick mitigation for customers: set max_concurrency to 16 and disable http2 multiplexing (sdk option: multiplex: false) until we patch the edge. Also reduce batch size to 64. Can we confirm disabling multiplexing avoids the 503s?

acmeops-customer: Trying the workaround now — disabling multiplexing and capping concurrency. Will report in ~5m.

oncall-bot: (automated) Incident created INC-2026-4873 assigned to eng-sre; paging oncall.

raj-eng-sre: Triage notes: observed many connection resets correlated with increased active streams per connection. Edge proxy's per-connection stream limit hit and then GOAWAYs cause upstream retry stream resets. Also saw NAT port reuse near limits on worker nodes. Hypothesis: very high multiplexing + large batches => long-lived streams + head-of-line queuing => upstream resets.

marta-eng-infra: Captured tcpdump on affected frontends, forwarded to storage: s3://redwood-debug/7165432100/pcap.tar.gz. Also instrumented an edge parameter to temporarily lower max streams per connection to force earlier connection rotation. Rolling change to us-west2 now (canary at 09:35).

acmeops-customer: After disabling multiplexing + capping concurrency to 16, 503s dropped to <1% within 2 minutes. Will keep under observation for 30m. Thanks.

emma-support: Noted customer confirmation — communicating status and recommended temp config.

raj-eng-sre: Next steps: 1) add a short-term mitigation in edge to smooth stream limits (in progress), 2) postmortem data capture for traffic patterns, 3) recommend SDK change to limit default concurrency or a client-side guard versus default unlimited multiplex.

kai-devex: I'll open a docs PR to add guidance: "large batch + http2 multiplexing can amplify retries and cause gateway 5xx; recommended defaults: batch <=64, max_concurrency 16, multiplex=false for bulk embed jobs."

marta-eng-infra: Canary shows reduced GOAWAYs and no spike in worker ephemeral ports. Will promote fix across us-west2 in 10m.

raj-eng-sre: Will monitor for 1h; if stable, we'll update the customer and close INC-2026-4873. Assigning follow-up to eng-runtime for a longer-term fix (adaptive stream limits + smarter connection pooling).

acmeops-customer: thanks team — appreciate the fast help.

emma-support: Customer update sent with workaround & ETA for full region fix. Closing loop here once SRE confirms stable. :thumbsup:
